title: Optimal positive end-expiratory pressure reduces right ventricular dysfunction in COVID-19 patients on venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: A retrospective single-center study
notes: Primary research. 69 VV-ECMO patients, single center (OHSU); groups defined by era (standard PEEP before Jan 2021 vs esophageal-manometry-guided optimal PEEP after). Effectively a before-after/era comparison analyzed as two arms. No overlap with other files identified.

title: Effects of different positive end-expiratory pressure titration strategies on mechanical power during ultraprotective ventilation in ARDS patients treated with veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: A prospective interventional study
notes: Primary research. 20 ARDS patients on VV-ECMO, three PEEP strategies applied sequentially in every patient. Same Mannheim group (Boesing/Krebs/Luecke) as s13054-022-03956-8 and s13054-024-04867-6; population here is ECMO patients so cohort overlap with those two is less likely but should be checked. Two Boesing 2024 papers in folder, hence suffix a/b.

title: Bedside personalized methods based on electrical impedance tomography or respiratory mechanics to set PEEP in ARDS and recruitment-to-inflation ratio: a physiologic study
notes: Primary research. 19 ARDS patients, University Hospital of Angers, Dec 2019-Apr 2020; four PEEP-titration strategies compared within each patient during a decremental PEEP trial. Text states the 10 COVID-ARDS patients were already included in a previously published study (their ref 14, not identified here). Strong suspicion of cohort/investigator overlap with s13054-025-05626-x (Chean 2025, same Angers unit, Pavlovsky is a co-author) - verify enrolment dates. Filename (S2110582025...) suggests 2025 but the article itself is dated 2024;14:1.

title: A lung rescue team improves survival in obesity with acute respiratory distress syndrome
notes: Primary research. Retrospective two-era cohort at MGH: standard protocol cohort 2012-2014 (n=70) vs lung rescue team cohort 2015-2017 (n=50), class III obesity. Same MGH Lung Rescue Team program as lung_recruitment_in_obese_patients_with_acute.25.pdf (Fumagalli 2019) and pirrone2016.pdf (Pirrone 2016); patient overlap plausible since those physiologic studies enrolled MGH obese ICU patients in overlapping years.

title: Mortality and pulmonary mechanics in relation to respiratory system and transpulmonary driving pressures in ARDS
notes: NOT an independent primary study - secondary/post hoc analysis. Abstract states 'Fifty-six patients from a previous study were analyzed'; comparison is intervention vs control of that trial. Companion paper in this folder: talmor2008.pdf (Talmor NEJM 2008 esophageal-pressure-guided PEEP trial, n=61, commonly called EPVent-1). Do not double-count with talmor_2008.

title: Effect of Titrating Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (PEEP) With an Esophageal Pressure-Guided Strategy vs an Empirical High PEEP-FiO2 Strategy on Death and Days Free From Mechanical Ventilation Among Patients With Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Randomized Clinical Trial
notes: Primary report of EPVent-2 (NCT01681225), phase 2 RCT, 14 North American hospitals, n=200. DUPLICATE COHORT: effect-of-esophageal-pressure-guided-positive-end-expiratory-pressure-on-survival-from-acute-respiratory-distress.pdf (Sarge 2021) is a post hoc reanalysis of these same 200 participants.

title: Transpulmonary Pressure-Guided Lung-Protective Ventilation Improves Pulmonary Mechanics and Oxygenation Among Obese Subjects on Mechanical Ventilation
notes: Primary research. Retrospective analysis of 20 obese subjects; ventilator settings/mechanics compared before vs 24 h after starting PL-guided ventilation in the same subjects (no separate control group). Respir Care 2021;66(7):1049-1058; no DOI printed on first page. Filename is an EBSCO export name and does not identify the paper.

title: Effect of Esophageal Pressure-guided Positive End-Expiratory Pressure on Survival from Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: A Risk-based and Mechanistic Reanalysis of the EPVent-2 Trial
journal: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
notes: NOT an independent primary study - explicitly a post hoc reanalysis of EPVent-2 including all 200 trial participants. DUPLICATE COHORT with beitler2019.pdf. First page also notes the article has a related editorial (editorial itself is not in this folder).

title: Positive End-Expiratory Pressure Setting in COVID-19-Related Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Comparison Between Electrical Impedance Tomography, PEEP/FiO2 Tables, and Transpulmonary Pressure
notes: Primary research, labelled 'Brief Research Report'. 17 COVID-ARDS patients (Nancy, France, March 2021); three PEEP-setting methods applied within each patient. Physiologic endpoints only, no clinical outcomes.

title: The potential risk of ventilator-induced lung injury from five different PEEP titration techniques in ARDS
notes: Primary research. 21 moderate-severe ARDS patients (Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok); recruitment maneuver then decremental PEEP trial with five optimal-PEEP criteria evaluated in each patient. Note first author listed as Sutherasan with co-first author Songsomboon.

title: ECMO criteria for influenza A (H1N1)-associated ARDS: role of transpulmonary pressure
notes: Primary research. Prospective data collection in 14 H1N1-ARDS patients referred for ECMO (Turin, Oct 2009-Jan 2010); esophageal manometry used to partition mechanics and to raise PEEP in the 7 patients with low PPLAT-L. Comparison is before/after PEEP increase within a subgroup, not a controlled comparison.

title: Utilizing Indirect Intrapleural Pressure to Guide Mechanical Ventilation in Burn Patients With ARDS
notes: Primary research (ABA annual meeting associated article). Retrospective review of 23 burn patients with ARDS at one burn center; ventilator settings and oxygenation compared before vs 1, 3 and 5 days after starting esophageal pressure monitoring. Single group, before-after design. First author surname is compound (Soo Ping Chow).

title: Lung Recruitment in Obese Patients with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
notes: Primary research. 14 severely obese ARDS patients; three PEEP titration strategies applied in fixed order in each patient. Authorship 'on behalf of the Lung Rescue Team Investigators' (MGH) - possible patient overlap with a-lung-rescue-team-improves-survival-in-obesity-with-acute-respi-2020.pdf (Florio 2020 lung rescue team cohort 2015-2017) and with pirrone2016.pdf (same MGH group, morbidly obese).

title: The impact of a lung-protective ventilation mode using transpulmonary driving pressure titrated positive end-expiratory pressure on the prognosis of patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome
journal: Journal of Clinical Monitoring and Computing
notes: Primary research. 105 ARDS patients randomly assigned to control (tidal-volume/plateau-based PEEP, n=51) vs transpulmonary driving pressure-guided PEEP (n=53), Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital; 28-day mortality, VAP, 60-day follow-up. Abstract says 'randomly assigned' but gives no randomization detail on page 1.

title: Medical effectiveness of esophageal balloon pressure manometry in weaning patients from mechanical ventilation
notes: Primary research but LIKELY OFF-TOPIC for a PEEP-titration review: it evaluates esophageal balloon monitoring to guide WEANING, not PEEP setting. Prospective study of 23 consecutive patients, each serving as his or her own control, two weaning strategies. Crit Care Med 1995;23:504-509. File is a plain-text database rendition (Ovid/EBSCO style), page 1 is a journal cover; citation read from page 2. No DOI shown. Funded in part by Bicore Monitoring Systems.

title: Effects of positive end-expiratory pressure strategy in supine and prone position on lung and chest wall mechanics in acute respiratory distress syndrome
notes: Primary research. Prospective physiologic study, 38 ARDS patients in two university ICUs (Lyon, Barcelona); PEEP/FiO2 table vs Pes-guided PEEP, each in supine and prone position, within the same patients. Similar question to the Mannheim prone papers (s13054-022-03956-8, s13054-024-04867-6) but a different, independent cohort.

title: Obesity and Weaning from Mechanical Ventilation-An Exploratory Study
journal: Clinical Medicine Insights: Circulatory, Respiratory and Pulmonary Medicine
notes: Primary research, pilot RCT. 25 morbidly obese tracheotomized subjects randomly assigned to esophageal-balloon-guided PEEP (ESO) vs best static compliance PEEP (Cstat); outcome is weaning by day 30. NCT02323009. East Carolina University.

title: Effect of different titration methods on right heart function and prognosis in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome
notes: Primary research. Observational prospective study, 62 ARDS patients allocated (not stated as randomized) to three PEEP-titration groups: guide (n=40), driving-pressure-oriented (n=12), transpulmonary-pressure-oriented (n=10). Shaanxi Provincial People's Hospital. Note the very unequal, non-randomized group sizes.

title: Recruitment Maneuvers and Positive End-Expiratory Pressure Titration in Morbidly Obese ICU Patients
notes: Primary research. Stated design: prospective, crossover, nonrandomized interventional study; 14 morbidly obese mechanically ventilated patients at Massachusetts General Hospital. Same MGH group/era as fumagalli_2019 and florio_2020 - check for patient overlap (all three are MGH obese ICU/ARDS populations, Berra/Kacmarek senior authors).

title: Positive end expiratory pressure titrated by transpulmonary pressure improved oxygenation and respiratory mechanics in acute respiratory distress syndrome patients with intra-abdominal hypertension
notes: Primary research. 15 ARDS patients (7 with and 8 without intra-abdominal hypertension) at Zhongda Hospital, Nanjing; each patient ventilated at two PEEP levels (Ptp-titrated and ARDSNet-titrated) with measurements after 30 min in each round. Filename does not identify author/year; article is Chin Med J 2013;126(17):3234-3239.

title: Retrospective Review of Transpulmonary Pressure Guided Positive End-Expiratory Pressure Titration for Mechanical Ventilation in Class II and III Obesity
notes: Primary research. Retrospective cohort of 29 obese (BMI >=35) ARDS patients in a community ICU in Newark, Delaware; PEEP, oxygenation and driving pressure compared before vs 4 h and 24 h after esophageal manometry (Wilcoxon signed rank). Single group, before-after, no control arm.

title: Personalized positive end-expiratory pressure in spontaneously breathing patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome by simultaneous electrical impedance tomography and transpulmonary pressure monitoring: a randomized crossover trial
notes: Primary research. Multicenter randomized crossover physiologic study, 30 intubated ARDS patients undergoing pressure support ventilation (Milan/Rome/Ferrara); PEEP-EIT-dPL vs PEEP-table, 20 min each. Overlapping Italian investigator network with scaramuzzo2020.pdf (Scaramuzzo, Spadaro, Mauri) but different population (PSV vs controlled ventilation) and different years - overlap unlikely but worth checking.

title: Effects of different positive end-expiratory pressure titration strategies during prone positioning in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome: a prospective interventional study
notes: Primary research. 40 consecutive moderate-severe ARDS patients, University Medical Centre Mannheim; three PEEP titration strategies evaluated in both supine and prone position within each patient. SUSPECTED COHORT OVERLAP with s13054-024-04867-6.pdf (Boesing 2024 Crit Care, 55 patients, same center, same prone/supine esophageal-pressure-guided protocol) - the 2024 sample may include these 40 patients.

title: Physiological effects of lung-protective ventilation in patients with lung fibrosis and usual interstitial pneumonia pattern versus primary ARDS: a matched-control study
notes: Primary research, labelled 'Brief Report'. 10 AE-ILD-UIP patients matched 1:1 with 10 primary ARDS controls (Modena/Bari); three PEEP levels (ZEEP, PEEP-LOW, PEEP-titrated) applied within each patient. Hybrid structure: within-patient PEEP steps plus a matched between-group comparison. Population is largely non-ARDS (interstitial lung disease), which may put it outside a standard ARDS eligibility frame.

title: Effects of prone positioning on lung mechanical power components in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome: a physiologic study
notes: Primary research. Prospective physiologic study, 55 moderate-severe ARDS patients, Mannheim; supine vs prone under esophageal-pressure-guided ventilation, plus comparison with an oxygenation-guided strategy in supine. SUSPECTED COHORT OVERLAP with s13054-022-03956-8.pdf (Boesing 2022, n=40, same center and protocol family). Second of two Boesing 2024 papers (see 1-s2.0-S0883944123001557-main.pdf = boesing_2024a).

title: Comparison of two transpulmonary pressure-based positive end-expiratory pressure titration strategies in acute respiratory distress syndrome: a randomized crossover study
notes: Primary research. Randomized crossover physiologic study, 20 moderate-severe ARDS patients in one academic ICU (Angers); directly measured expiratory PL vs elastance-derived inspiratory PL strategy, 45 min each with washout. SUSPECTED INVESTIGATOR/COHORT OVERLAP with 1-s2.0-S2110582025001499-main.pdf (Pavlovsky 2024, same Angers unit, shared authors Pavlovsky, Desprez, Richard, Mercat, Beloncle) - check enrolment windows before counting both.

title: Personalized Positive End-Expiratory Pressure in Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Comparison Between Optimal Distribution of Regional Ventilation and Positive Transpulmonary Pressure
notes: Primary research. Stated design: cross-over prospective physiologic study; 20 ARDS patients in two academic ICUs (Ferrara, Milan); PEEP-PL vs PEEP-EIT titration trials in randomized cross-over order, 20 min each. Shares senior authors with s00134-024-07695-y.pdf (Mauri 2024) - different population, overlap unlikely.

title: Managing Hypercapnia in Patients with Severe ARDS and Low Respiratory System Compliance: The Role of Esophageal Pressure Monitoring - A Case Cohort Study
notes: Primary research but very small and uncontrolled: 6 patients with severe ARDS and hypercapnia; PEEP and driving pressure adjusted using transpulmonary pressure, PaCO2 and mechanics compared before vs 1 h after intervention. Self-described 'case cohort study'; effectively a case series. Article ID 385042.

title: Mechanical Ventilation Guided by Esophageal Pressure in Acute Lung Injury
notes: Primary report of the single-center pilot RCT (NCT00127491) of esophageal-pressure-guided PEEP vs ARDSNet control, n=61, stopped after reaching its stopping criterion; widely referred to as EPVent-1 though no acronym appears on page 1. DUPLICATE COHORT: baedorfkassis2016.pdf re-analyzes 56 of these patients.

title: Evaluation of Esophageal Pressures in Mechanically Ventilated Obese Patients
notes: NOT an interventional study of PEEP titration - retrospective database analysis of the MIMIC-III critical care database (105 subjects) comparing esophageal pressures in obese vs non-obese subjects, with the EPVent-2 PEEP protocols applied only THEORETICALLY (simulated, not delivered). Likely ineligible if the review requires an applied PEEP-titration intervention. Cohort is MIMIC-III, so no overlap with the trial papers, but it re-uses EPVent-2 protocol definitions from beitler2019.pdf.

title: A clinical study on mechanical ventilation PEEP setting for traumatic ARDS patients guided by esophageal pressure
notes: Primary research. 23 traumatic ARDS patients randomly divided into esophageal-pressure-guided PEEP (n=12) and ARDSNet PEEP/FiO2 table (n=11) groups; Xiamen Third Hospital. CAUTION: this PDF is an uncorrected galley proof watermarked 'unpublished proof version', header reads 'Technology and Health Care -1 (2018) 1-11'; the filename says 2019, so the final published year/volume/pages may differ from the year recorded here. First author Bing Wang - distinct from wang2020.pdf (Rui Wang), so no letter suffix needed.

title: Mechanical Ventilation Strategy Guided by Transpulmonary Pressure in Severe Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Treated With Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation
notes: Primary research. Single-center prospective RCT, Beijing Chao-Yang Hospital; 104 severe ARDS patients on VV-ECMO randomized to transpulmonary pressure-guided ventilation (n=52) vs lung rest (n=52), 102 analyzed. First author Rui Wang (different person from wang2019.pdf, Bing Wang).

filename: World j  surg - 2025 - Zhao - Individualized Lung‐Protective Ventilation Strategy Based on Esophageal Pressure Monitoring.pdf
title: Individualized Lung-Protective Ventilation Strategy Based on Esophageal Pressure Monitoring in Patients With ARDS Associated With Severe Acute Pancreatitis-A Randomized Controlled Trial
notes: Primary research. RCT of 124 patients with severe-acute-pancreatitis-associated ARDS (Jan-Dec 2023), randomized to conventional lung-protective ventilation (n=62) vs esophageal-pressure-monitoring-guided ventilation (n=62); reports 28-day mortality, VAP, ventilation duration. Filename contains spaces and a non-ASCII hyphen.

title: Setting PEEP in patients with COVID-19-related ARDS: a physiological comparison between methods
notes: Search update 2026-09-29 (U0023). Post hoc analysis of 29 COVID-ARDS patients from two Dutch hospital cohorts (Erasmus MC); one decremental PEEP trial per patient, recommended PEEP by EIT crossing point, positive PL,EE and best Crs compared within patient, with PL,EE, collapse and overdistension at each. Decision-level comparison like pavlovsky_2024 and sutherasan_2025. No overlap with other files identified.

title: The Effect of Transpulmonary Pressure-Guided Positive End-Expiratory Pressure Titration on Pulmonary Arterial Compliance in Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Patients: A Single-Center, Randomized Controlled Pilot Pathophysiological Study
notes: Search update 2026-09-29 (U0069). 40 pneumonia-ARDS patients, Beijing Chao-Yang Hospital, 2023-24, NCT05629832; PEEP to expiratory Ptp 0-5 cmH2O (n=20) vs empirical low tidal volume (n=20); pulmonary arterial compliance, RV function, oxygen delivery over 72 h. Different centre from sun_2024 (Shanghai).

title: Comparison of PEEP titration methods to improve respiratory system compliance in acute respiratory distress syndrome: a randomized controlled study
notes: Search update 2026-09-29 (U0084). Four-arm RCT, 49 ARDS patients, Hospital Nereu Ramos, Florianopolis, 2018-21, REBEC RBR-9b7jbxm: EIT 12, esophageal catheter 13, best compliance 12, low PEEP/FiO2 table 12. Eligible contrast: catheter vs PEEP/FiO2 table. File = article (pages 1-14) + supplementary material (pages 15-23) merged: 28-day mortality, VFD, LOS, barotrauma by arm are only in supplementary Table 4S.
